messages.author: 9929ba9eeb4bf762
messages.subject: Flipping X/Y axes
parts:
Hi,

I noticed that the plot.neuron function as axes options of “XY”, “YZ”, “XZ”, “ZY”. Though I would want to flip axes for XY (e.g. YX), how would I be able to do this?

Best,
Ken

messages.author: 7e98b49586f8806c
messages.subject: Re: Flipping X/Y axes
parts:
Hi Ken,

The coordinate data of the skeleton nodes is stored in `neuron$d`, assuming `neuron` is the variable name for your neuron. One trick you can do is to swap the `X` and `Y` columns there. Then when you plot axes = "XY", you'll be in fact plotting the "YX" view.

Best,
arthur

messages.author: 7f0257cd1389289f
messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] Re: Flipping X/Y axes
parts:
Thanks, Arthur!

Ken, thanks for your interest. Some other suggestions:

You can use xform to apply arbitrary transformations to your neuron or group of neurons. This could include a rotation matrix defined by rgl.

You can make it easier to swap columns by using the xyzmatrix function. For example this will swap x and y for a neuron or neuronlist, n:

xyzmatrix(n)=xyzmatrix(n)[,c(2,1,3)]

I don’t think there is currently a way to swap the plot axes since we only support base R plots in 2D. It would however be very simple to give PlotAxes additional options if you file a GitHub issue.

Of course you can do plot3d and choose any orientation you like eg with nview3d.

Best,

Greg.

http://natverse.org/nat/reference/xform.html
https://rdrr.io/rforge/rgl/man/matrices.html
